identification.summary: Financially motivated cluster that Microsoft tracks as Storm-0569 (formerly DEV-0569). Microsoft describes it as an access broker that distributes the BATLOADER downloader and other post-compromise payloads, and assessed in 2022 that its widespread infections and diverse payloads likely make it an attractive access broker for ransomware operators [S1][S2].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft reported BATLOADER distribution by DEV-0569 from August to October 2022 [S1]; it also states the actor moved away from ZLoader in early 2022 [S1]. Microsoft observed App Installer-based activity by several financially motivated actors, including Storm-0569, since mid-November 2023 [S2].
identification.notes: DEV-0569 was a temporary designation for an emerging cluster; in April 2023 Microsoft renamed it Storm-0569 [S1]. The encyclopedia record carries country code 'FIN', which here appears to denote 'financially motivated' rather than a country; no source gathered gives a nationality [S3]. Other vendors' names for this cluster were not found in sources gathered.

attribution.confidence: Microsoft calls DEV-0569 'likely' an attractive access broker for ransomware operators (2022) and later describes Storm-0569 as an access broker [S1][S2]. No government attribution and no nationality assessment was found.
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and analysis of infection chains [S1][S2].

objectives: Financial gain by selling or handing off access: Microsoft says Storm-0569 downloads post-compromise payloads such as BATLOADER, supplies malicious installers and landing-page frameworks to other actors, and hands access to ransomware operators [S2]. In 2022 its chains also delivered the Vidar stealer and Gozi banking trojan [S1].

targeting.notes: Microsoft names no victim industries or organizations in either post; targets are users searching for or receiving links to popular software (Zoom, Tableau, TeamViewer, AnyDesk), and recipients of phishing emails [S1][S2]. In September 2022 the actor sent messages through targets' website contact forms posing as a national financial authority [S1].

capabilities.summary: Initial access through malvertising, SEO poisoning of spoofed software landing pages, phishing emails, fake forum pages and blog comments [S1][S2]. Lures spoof Microsoft Teams, Zoom, TeamViewer, Adobe Flash Player and AnyDesk, hosted on lookalike domains and on GitHub and OneDrive, with legitimately signed files that use MSI Custom Actions to launch PowerShell or batch scripts [S1]. In October 2022 it abused Google Ads redirecting to the Keitaro traffic distribution system, which filtered by IP range and evaded sandboxes; Microsoft reported the abuse to Google [S1]. It used NSudo to try to disable antivirus and NirCmd to elevate to SYSTEM [S1]. Payloads included BATLOADER, Cobalt Strike Beacon, Vidar, Gozi, IcedID and RMM tools, with Rclone for exfiltration [S1][S2]. From late 2023 it abused the ms-appinstaller URI scheme and malicious signed MSI files [S2].

campaigns.name: Contact-form impersonation of a financial authority
campaigns.summary: DEV-0569 sent messages via targets' website contact forms posing as a national financial authority and replied to respondents with BATLOADER links; payloads included Gozi and Vidar [S1].

campaigns.name: BATLOADER to Royal ransomware chains
campaigns.summary: Microsoft found DEV-0569 infection chains leading to human-operated attacks deploying Royal ransomware, with ransomware operators likely entering through a BATLOADER-delivered Cobalt Strike Beacon [S1].

campaigns.name: Google Ads malvertising via Keitaro
campaigns.summary: Malvertising used Google Ads pointing to Keitaro TDS, which sent most users to a legitimate download site and, under conditions, to the BATLOADER site; reported to Google [S1].

campaigns.name: App Installer abuse and SEO poisoning
campaigns.summary: From mid-November 2023 (per Microsoft's December 2023 post) Storm-0569 used spoofed software landing pages in Bing and Google results, phishing links and ms-appinstaller prompts to deliver BATLOADER; in one instance BATLOADER dropped Cobalt Strike, Rclone exfiltrated data, and Storm-0506 deployed Black Basta. Microsoft says access is handed to Storm-0846 and Storm-0506 [S2].

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated access broker tracked by Microsoft as Storm-0569; identity and nationality not stated in sources [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: BATLOADER, Cobalt Strike, Vidar, Gozi, IcedID, RMM tools, Rclone, NSudo, NirCmd; malvertising, SEO poisoning, phishing, App Installer abuse [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Lookalike domains, GitHub and OneDrive hosting, Keitaro TDS behind Google Ads, spoofed software landing pages; Microsoft lists Storm-0506 Cobalt Strike C2 domains gertefin[.]com and septcntr[.]com for the downstream chain [S1][S2].
diamond.victim: Users and organizations seeking popular software or receiving phishing links; no sectors named [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Cybercriminal access-broker economy feeding ransomware affiliates (Royal-linked chains in 2022, Black Basta via Storm-0506 in 2023) [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints where users download installers, trust signed MSI files, or accept App Installer prompts; search engines and ad platforms as delivery channels [S1][S2].

gaps: No victim sectors, regions or counts are published in the sources gathered [S1][S2].
Activity after December 2023 was not found; current status is unknown.
Handoff relationships with Storm-0846 and Storm-0506 come from a single Microsoft post; Storm-0846 was not researched [S2].
Secondary catalogs (MISP galaxy, Malpedia, Strobes) repeat the Storm-0569 to Storm-0506 to Black Basta chain, but they were not fetchable or dated and are not cited.
Which ransomware operators received access in the 2022 Royal chains is not stated by Microsoft; Royal is said to be distributed by multiple actors [S1].
Encyclopedia record country code 'FIN' is unexplained and unsupported by sources.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: User endpoints that download software, and the search and ad ecosystems that steer them, are the key terrain; this is a commodity-crime entry vector into any network including DoD-adjacent contractors [S1][S2]. STEP 2: Signed installers, MSI Custom Actions and legitimate hosting (GitHub, OneDrive) defeat reputation-based blocking [S1]. STEP 3: Template is malvertising or SEO lure, then BATLOADER, then Cobalt Strike or RMM, then handoff to a ransomware crew [S1][S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued access brokering feeding ransomware affiliates against any exposed organization. MDCOA is a ransomware-ready foothold on a mission-relevant network sold to an actor that disrupts operations. Candidate indicators: ms-appinstaller launches from browsers, MSI-spawned PowerShell, NSudo use, Rclone to unfamiliar cloud storage, unauthorized RMM tools [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track ransomware-linked broker activity and the time between BATLOADER execution and hands-on-keyboard actions [S2]. (2) Authorities: blocking ms-appinstaller and software-install policy are local configuration decisions that should be set in advance [S2]. (3) Mission assurance: reduce user ability to install software from the web and keep offline backups for mission systems [S1]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3 and DIB partners and report malvertising abuse to ad platforms, as Microsoft did to Google [S1].
